taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Opiro, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 54.639 | 0.2147 | 0.2147
2 | 9147.8 | 0.30305 | 0.51774
3 | 1119.9 | 21.107 | 21.625
4 | 2566.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Opiro, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Opiro, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Opiro yields a four-layer resistivity model. Layer 1 is a thin, low-resistivity topsoil/weathered zone (54.6 Ω·m, 0.21 m thick), underlain by a very thin but highly resistive layer 2 (9147.8 Ω·m, 0.30 m thick), likely a compact or lateritic unit. Layer 3 is a thick, moderately resistive zone (1119.9 Ω·m, ~21.1 m), interpreted as a weathered/fractured aquiferous formation, followed by layer 4, the basement/half-space, with resistivity 2566.8 Ω·m.

Applying curve-type logic: layers 1-2-3 (54.6 < 9147.8 > 1119.9) give a K-type segment, while layers 2-3-4 (9147.8 > 1119.9 < 2566.8) give an H-type segment. This produces a combined **KH** curve, consistent with the resistivity sequence.

The classification on file matches the computed curve type based on the given resistivity values.

{"curve_type_stated": "KH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
